story.title: Jensen Huang Returns as Nvidia CEO Following Controversial Resignation
story.summary: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its President and CEO, just days after he resigned amid allegations of extramarital affairs and connections to a Chinese intelligence asset. The board's decision, influenced by advocacy from US President Donald Trump, has led to a significant surge in Nvidia's stock price. Huang's return has sparked discussions about potential investigations into the circumstances surrounding his resignation.

event_overview.title: About Nvidia Leadership
event_overview.subject: Nvidia Leadership
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a leadership transition at NVIDIA after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive officer and a board member, effective immediately. NVIDIA’s board installed Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor; the selected timeline also includes Huang’s subsequent public willingness to return if the board chooses.

facts.label: Leadership transition date
facts.value: NVIDIA’s board accepted Jen-Hsun Huang’s resignation on November 11, 2026, effective immediately; the company publicly announced the transition on November 12, 2026.

facts.label: Interim chief executive
facts.value: Colette M. Kress, NVIDIA’s executive vice president and chief financial officer since 2013, was appointed interim CEO and continues to hold the CFO role during the interim period.

facts.label: Successor process
facts.value: NVIDIA’s board said it is conducting a search for a permanent CEO and will consider both internal and external candidates.

facts.label: Huang’s tenure
facts.value: Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and had served as its president, CEO and a director since the company’s inception before the November 2026 transition.

facts.label: Board leadership
facts.value: The board appointed Harvey C. Jones as NVIDIA’s first chair of the board as part of the transition announcement.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the resignation and the later indication that Huang could return as CEO, not a comprehensive record of NVIDIA’s operations, financial performance, board deliberations or all related reporting.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed at Nvidia?
explore_lenses.title: A unanimous board reversal restored Huang
explore_lenses.summary: Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director effective November 22, reversing the November 12 resignation and ending Colette Kress’s interim tenure as CEO.

claims.text: Nvidia’s November 23 Form 8-K says the board reinstated Jen-Hsun Huang effective immediately on November 22, 2026.
The company said directors voted unanimously after discussions with Huang and were satisfied with his candor and ability to lead Nvidia.
Kress remains Nvidia’s executive vice president and CFO following Huang’s return; she had been named interim CEO when he resigned on November 12.

explore_lenses.label: How did the White House factor in?
explore_lenses.title: Government input was central to the reversal
explore_lenses.summary: Nvidia said it received senior-level U.S. government input before reinstating Huang. President Trump publicly supported the outcome, while the company framed its decision as consistent with national-security assurances.

claims.text: Nvidia said that, based on input from senior levels of the U.S. government, its board was confident Huang’s reinstatement posed no national-security risk.
Trump said he had spoken with Huang and that his administration had assured Nvidia there were no national-security concerns with Huang returning, according to the Associated Press.
Nvidia shares rose about 33% in early trading after the reinstatement announcement, Reuters reported; that was an intraday market move, not a final closing-price measure.

explore_lenses.summary: Huang’s return does not itself close the company’s independent review or settle possible government scrutiny. Public records show an independent-director investigation and congressional requests for federal investigation, but no published final findings.

claims.text: On November 8, Nvidia said an independent-director committee, assisted by outside counsel, would investigate reporting that Huang had been targeted by a foreign-intelligence effort.
At the start of that review, Nvidia said it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets had been compromised, while saying the inquiry would examine all available information.

Representatives Josh Gottheimer and Darin LaHood asked the FBI to investigate the publicly reported relationship and related possible PRC-intelligence links; the letter is a request for action, not evidence that the FBI reached a conclusion.
Nvidia’s November 17 earnings release still identified its independent-board investigation and possible government or regulatory inquiries as matters carrying uncertainty.

story_report.summary: Nvidia reinstated Jen-Hsun Huang as president and chief executive, effective Nov. 22, days after his resignation amid allegations involving affairs and espionage concerns. The board acted unanimously after discussions with Huang and said it was satisfied with his candor and leadership ability. President Donald Trump had advocated for Huang’s return, while Nvidia said input from senior U.S. officials gave the board confidence that reinstatement posed no national-security risk. Nvidia shares rose about 33% in early trading after the announcement.

sections.heading: Nvidia Board Restores Huang Leadership
sections.body: Huang had resigned on Nov. 12, when Nvidia named executive vice president and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. Following his reinstatement, Kress remained in her CFO role. Nvidia’s Nov. 23 filing said the board restored Huang immediately, while the company’s press release said directors had voted unanimously after speaking with him.

sections.heading: Huang Intelligence Review Remains Unfinished
sections.body: Nvidia said on Nov. 8 that an independent-director committee, aided by outside counsel, would examine reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign-intelligence effort. The company initially said it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets had been compromised, but said the review would assess all available information. Representatives Josh Gottheimer and Darin LaHood separately asked the FBI to investigate publicly reported relationship and possible PRC-intelligence links; their letter did not establish an FBI conclusion.

unresolved.text: Nvidia has not publicly detailed the board’s internal deliberations beyond its stated rationale for restoring Huang.

No public final report from Nvidia’s independent committee or definitive public finding by a law-enforcement agency had been located as of Nov. 24, 2026; Nvidia had also identified possible government or regulatory inquiries as uncertain.
The underlying U.S. government assessments and the substance of communications with Nvidia’s board have not been publicly released.

related_stories.title: U.S. Places Megaspeed on Trade Blacklist Amid Nvidia Scandal
related_stories.summary: The U.S. government has added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist, citing the firm's alleged connections to espionage and its role in the Nvidia scandal. This decision follows scrutiny over the company's ties to China and its controlling shareholder, Alice Huang, who has been implicated in an espionage investigation. The announcement coincided with the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia.
